title: Algebraic Speedups for Exact Inversion of Hamiltonian Evolutions
authors: Jizhe Lai, Mingrui Jing, Erdong Huang, Xin Wang
abstract: Deterministic exact inversion of an arbitrary $d$-dimensional unitary requires {$Θ(d^2)$} coherent forward calls in the worst case. We ask how this cost changes for Hamiltonian evolution $U(x)=\exp(i\sum_j x_jH_j)$ when the generators are known but the parameters are hidden. For one-parameter families with a fixed eigenbasis, we show that additive relations among the distinct eigenvalues determine the optimal query number exactly, and we construct the corresponding inversion protocol. For general families, we prove that repeated symmetry sectors do not affect the exact query complexity and give an automatic construction for combining inverses from inequivalent active sectors. We also give a sufficient phase-alignment condition under which family-specific structure can reduce the query number. These results establish structure-dependent bounds for reversing the unknown dynamics arising in Tavis-Cummings out-of-time-order correlator protocols, collective-spin echo verification, and passive multimode links, without requiring prior knowledge or explicit estimation of the underlying coupling strengths.
summary: This paper develops structural theorems to determine the minimum number of forward quantum calls needed to exactly invert a unitary evolution generated by a known Hamiltonian. By exploiting algebraic properties like commutativity and sector decomposition, the authors show that the required query complexity can be drastically reduced compared to treating the system as an arbitrary black box. This has direct implications for optimizing quantum sensing protocols in areas like cavity QED and quantum optics.
main_problem: The core problem is determining the minimum number of forward quantum calls required to deterministically invert an unknown unitary evolution $U(x) = \exp(i\sum x_j H_j)$ when only the generators ($H_j$) are known, but the parameters ($\mathbf{x}$) are hidden.
main_result: For commuting Hamiltonians, the inversion cost depends on additive relations among distinct eigenvalues. For general noncommuting families, the complexity is bounded by a product structure derived from inverting inequivalent active sectors.
method: The authors analyze the algebraic structure of the Hamiltonian generators, utilizing techniques like Wedderburn decomposition to simplify the problem into independent, invertible blocks. They derive explicit bounds based on spectral properties and sector combination rules.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on general time-evolution $U(x) = \exp(i\sum x_j H_j)$, applied specifically to protocols involving Tavis-Cummings dynamics, collective spins (Ising/LMG), and passive multimode links in quantum optics.
key_observables: The primary observable is the minimum query number ($q$) required for exact inversion; other key observables include residual phases ($ho_\alpha(x)$) and the structure of joint-eigenvalue vectors ($\Lambda$).
important_parameters: The complexity scales with system dimension ($d$), mode numbers ($M, N$), and the number of emitters/spins ($n$). Structure-dependent bounds are shown to be polynomial in these parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes knowledge of the Hamiltonian generators $\{H_j\}$ and relies on algebraic structures like commutativity or decomposability into inequivalent sectors.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the general concept of structured Hamiltonian inversion using interleaved forward calls to implement $U(x)^\dagger$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the worst-case exponential cost for arbitrary unitaries. It then develops specialized results for commuting families based on eigenvalue sums, followed by a treatment for noncommuting generators using sector decomposition and phase alignment conditions.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous theoretical bounds on quantum control tasks (like echo verification or OTOC measurement reversal) that are crucial for understanding the resource cost of retrieving unknown system parameters from limited forward measurements.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Structured Hamiltonian inversion. The Hamil- tonian generators Hj and their algebraic relations are known, while their coefficients xj are hidden. A fixed quantum circuit interleaves q forward calls to U(x) = eiH(x) with parameter- independent gates and implements U(x)† up to a global phase, while restoring all auxiliary registers. The resulting inverse can be used in Loschmidt echoes, echo verification, and out- of-time-order correlator protocols.

FIG. 2. Query hierarchy for a passive multimode link. The horizontal axis gives the number n of optical modes, the vertical axis is logarithmic, and N denotes the photon- number cutoff. The dimension-only curve treats the full at- most-n-photon Hilbert space as an arbitrary unitary. The four arbitrary-X curves show constructive upper bounds for the indicated values of N. For N = 2, translation-invariant couplings around a ring and the rank-one bright-mode family give the exact values q = n and q = 2, respectively. The widening separation shows how additional structure changes the scaling from exponential to polynomial, and then to linear or constant.
